title: Load a Charpy specimen notch away from the striker, centred and square on the anvils
instruction: Load the Charpy specimen into the impact tester: lay it across the two supports, square against both anvils, with its notch facing away from the striker (its side is marked by the red strip) and centred between the anvils. Then let go of it and move clear of it.
context: Charpy impact tests (ASTM E23, ISO 148-1) are run every day by materials-testing technicians in weld-procedure qualification, steel-mill and pressure-vessel quality labs. The notched bar is laid on the machine's two supports, square against its two anvils, with the notch centred between them and facing away from the striker: the hammer hits the plain back face at mid-span and the bar breaks through the notch. A bar loaded notch toward the striker, off centre or standing off an anvil gives an invalid absorbed-energy value and a retest. The bar is placed with tongs, and they are withdrawn before the pendulum is released. Here the bar starts lying with its notch to one side, so it has to be turned a quarter turn the right way, and which way is right depends only on where the striker is. The pendulum is latched up out of the way (not modelled).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 2:1 bench mock-up of a pendulum impact (Charpy) tester's specimen area stands on the midline; everything except the specimen is fixed to the table. (1) Tester base: a dark grey cast-iron block, 140 mm (x) by 220 mm (y), 30 mm tall, spanning x 27.0-41.0 cm and y -11.0 to +11.0 cm. (2) Two supports: light grey hardened-steel blocks, 30 mm (x) by 35 mm (y), 10 mm tall, on the base at x 30.0-33.0 cm, one at y +4.0 to +7.5 cm and one at y -4.0 to -7.5 cm; their tops are 40 mm above the table. (3) Two anvils: light grey hardened-steel blocks, 20 mm (x) by 35 mm (y), 40 mm tall, on the base right behind the supports at x 33.0-35.0 cm, at the same y as the supports. Their faces toward the arms are at x 33.0 cm, flush with the supports' far edges, and rise 30 mm above the supports' tops; their inner edges are 80 mm apart (y -4.0 and +4.0 cm), twice the standard 40 mm span, so the midplane between them is y 0. (4) Striker mark: a red painted strip, 25 mm (x) by 8 mm (y), 1 mm thick, on the base's top centred at x 28.25 cm, y 0, in front of the gap between the supports: the side the striker comes from. (5) Mat: black rubber, 140 mm (x) by 50 mm (y), 3 mm thick, centred at x 20.0 cm, y -22.0 cm. (6) Specimen, loose: a 2:1 aluminium Charpy bar, 110 x 20 x 20 mm, 0.118 kg, pale silver-grey, lighter than the steel blocks (the standard bar is 55 x 10 x 10 mm). Across the middle of one of its four 110 x 20 mm long faces runs the notch, a square slot 4 mm wide and 4 mm deep over the full 20 mm height (a 2:1 stand-in for the 2 mm V-notch); a black tick, 4 x 6 mm and 0.5 mm thick, is painted on its top face just behind the notch. It lies flat on the mat with its length along x, centred at x 20.0 cm, y -22.0 cm, the notched face toward -y (away from the midline), tick up. The bar's top and bottom faces are alike apart from the tick. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the specimen's pose and both grippers (in a real trial: a steel rule, a 1.5 mm feeler gauge and a top photo). 'On the supports': the notch's 20 mm length within 5 degrees of vertical (either face up), the bar's length within 10 degrees of the line between the anvils (y) seen from above, and each end at least 3 mm past its support's inner edge, its centre line over the support (x 30.0-33.0 cm) and its underside within 2 mm of the support's top. 'Notch away': the notched face's outward normal within 30 degrees of +x (toward the anvils, away from the red strip). 'Offset' d: the distance along y from the centre of the notch's mouth to the midplane between the anvils (half the difference of the two rule readings from each anvil's inner edge to the notch). 'Anvil gap': at each anvil, the widest gap between its face and the bar's notched face, at mid-height, over the part of the bar in front of it (where a 1.5 mm feeler gauge would enter). 'At rest': neither end of the bar moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. 'Let go': each gripper's fingers at least 20 mm from the bar (a gripper's fingers are taken as everything within reach of a pad's outer corner around the 38 mm stretch back from the point between its pad tips: half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across, up to 57 mm when fully open). Score 0 if the bar is not at rest, not let go, or not on the supports (held, propped, on its side, standing on an end, on the anvils' tops, down on the base or table, crosswise), if its notch is not away (toward the striker or any other way), or if d is over 8 mm (the striker would land more than 8 mm from the notch). Otherwise 0.5, plus 0.25 if d is 2 mm or less (the two rule readings differ by 4 mm or less), plus 0.25 if both anvil gaps are 1.5 mm or less (square against both anvils: the feeler enters at neither). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75 (centred but standing off an anvil, or against both anvils with the notch 2-8 mm off centre), 1.0 (success, held 1 s). Every pose scored above 0 rests on both supports by itself: 8 mm off centre, each end still reaches 7 mm onto its support. Tick up or tick down scores the same.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The tester is a 2:1 mock-up made of fixed blocks: no pendulum, striker, latch or centring tongs (the pendulum is taken as latched up). The specimen is one rigid aluminium body of three blocks and a thin painted tick, its notch a 4 x 4 mm square slot instead of a V. The scorer reads only the specimen's pose and each gripper's position and opening, not contact forces.
reset_notes: Put the specimen back on the black mat centred at x 20.0 cm, y -22.0 cm, lying flat with its length along x, the notched face toward -y (away from the midline) and the tick up. Nothing is consumed; everything else is fixed.
